key_insight: AgentSkillOS provides a principled two-stage framework—organize skills into a capability tree and then retrieve+orchestrate them to solve tasks—enabling scalable discovery, selection, and ecosystem-level management of agent skills.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of discovering, selecting, composing, and benchmarking a rapidly growing number of agent skills (e.g., Claude skills) so practitioners can reliably reuse and scale skill-based agent workflows across an ecosystem.
method: Manage Skills: build a node-level recursive capability tree that categorizes skills for efficient discovery, registration, and lifecycle management.
Solve Tasks: retrieve relevant skills from the capability tree, orchestrate and compose them via a planner/selector pipeline to execute tasks end-to-end.
Ecosystem benchmarking: define metrics and workflows to evaluate skill coverage, composition success, and system-level performance across many skills.
impact: Makes large skill libraries practical to use by improving discoverability, automating orchestration, and providing ecosystem-level evaluation—reducing engineering overhead and accelerating deployment of multi-skill agent solutions.
visual_elements: Capability tree diagram showing recursive categorization of skills (nodes = categories, leaves = skill modules).
Pipeline flowchart: retrieval → planner/selector → orchestration → execution, annotated with decision points and metrics.
Benchmark dashboard mockup (heatmap/time-series) comparing skill coverage, composition success rate, and latency across the ecosystem.
Icon set illustrating skill lifecycle: register, discover, compose, evaluate.
paper_title: Organizing, Orchestrating, and Benchmarking Agent Skills at Ecosystem Scale
paper_authors: Hao Li, Chunjiang Mu, Jianhao Chen, Siyue Ren, Zhiyao Cui
